universal_lens: Homography-based pose-graph construction enables calibrated camera pose estimation through planar surface decomposition and real-line embedding pruning. The structural unification relies on projecting confidence-weighted relative pose estimates onto the Riemannian manifolds SO(3) and S^2. This geometric averaging minimizes embedding inconsistency across a bi-connected graph, ensuring global rigidity by enforcing least-unsquared-deviations constraints over multi-planar homography decompositions.
gsi_mapping: Bayesian inference on homography reliability integrates with conformal prediction for robust camera pose recovery under uncertain planar geometry. GSI maps these manifold projections to Bayesian posterior inference over spatial priors. Confidence weights act as conformal scores derived from planar invariance, while the spanning tree extension enforces topological consistency, minimizing epistemic uncertainty in high-dimensional camera state spaces.
gse_mapping: Situation-aware state transitions in pose-graph pruning leverage geometric consistency scores to refine camera pose estimates dynamically. In GSE, this primitive models situational transitions during dynamic plays. Relative poses represent instantaneous player-to-player vectors; aggregating noisy edge estimates via SO(3) projection yields robust, real-time formation tracking, filtering out occlusions and erratic movements on the court.

reasoning_traces.think: The mathematical derivation within pages 6-8 centers on the rigorous transition from local, noisy pairwise observations to a globally consistent Euclidean reconstruction. The foundational premise is the extraction of multiple independent relative poses (R, c) from distinct planar homographies between image pairs. Because these relative poses are invariant to the specific underlying plane generating the homography, they can be treated as stochastic samples from a distribution centered on the true geometric relationship. The core operator involves a weighted Fréchet mean on the Riemannian product manifold SO(3) × S². By projecting the confidence-weighted sum of raw rotations onto SO(3) and translations onto S², the method inherently respects the non-Euclidean geometry of rotations and directions, avoiding the severe biases introduced by naive Euclidean averaging. Once these robust edge weights are established on a minimal-range spanning tree, the algorithm addresses the fundamental lack of redundancy in trees. A tree structure is not bi-connected, meaning it cannot absorb gross errors or resolve global scale ambiguities effectively. The extension to a bi-connected graph via iterative edge addition—specifically targeting those that minimize embedding inconsistency—acts as a topological regularization. This process constructs a dense constraint network. Finally, the absolute positions are recovered via Least-Unsquared-Deviations (LUD). LUD is particularly apt here as it optimizes the alignment of relative difference vectors (c_i - c_j) in a way that is robust to outliers, completing the transformation from a probabilistic graph of local planes to a deterministic, global 3D camera configuration. This pipeline elegantly bridges differential geometry and combinatorial optimization.
